summary: Paul Tedesco was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and linguistic studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna under Bernhard Geiger. He held positions at the Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton University, and Yale University.

Paul Theodor Hoffmann worked in Indology, philosophy, and other fields. He studied at Munich, Berlin, Grenoble Alpes, and Tübingen, where he earned his Ph.D. under Richard von Garbe. In 1941, he was director of the Theaterwissenschaftliches Institut at Hamburg.

Indologist and linguist Paul Thieme studied at Göttingen under Emil Sieg, in Berlin under Heinrich Lüders and Wilhelm Schulze, and under Kamalakanta Mishra. His academic posts included professorships at Halle-Wittenberg, Frankfurt, Yale (1954–1960), and Tübingen (1960–1973).

Paul Tillich was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Breslau. He held professorships at TU Dresden, Leipzig, and Frankfurt before moving to Union Theological Seminary, Harvard University, and the University of Chicago.

Paul W. Kroll is a Sinologist who completed his studies at the University of Michigan around 1969–1976. Around 1979, he served as Associate Professor of Chinese and department chair at the University of Colorado Boulder.

Paul Whalley was an Indologist and historian who earned his B.A. and M.A. at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served in the Bengal Civil Service from 1860 to 1890 and was Secretary at the Ministry of Home Affairs from 1871 to 1872.
Paul Wilfred O'Brien worked in Buddhist studies, earning his Ph.D. from the University of California, Berkeley by 1941. He later taught at the Pontifical College of St. Pius X from 1958 to 1965.

Paul Williams specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Sussex and the University of Oxford. His career includes a research fellowship at Wadham College and serving as Professor of Indian and Tibetan Philosophy at the University of Bristol.
Paul Wodilla was an Indologist who studied at Comenius University and received his Ph.D. from the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg by 1928.

Paul de Lagarde was a scholar of religious studies, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and Halle-Wittenberg under August Tholuck and Friedrich Rückert, later serving as professor at the University of Göttingen from 1869.
Paul-Abel Sabbathier was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Abel Bergaigne and Ferdinand de Saussure.

Indologist Paul-Émile Dumont studied at Brussels, Bologna, and under teachers including Francesco Lorenzo Pullè, Willem Caland, Hermann Oldenberg, and Paul Deussen. He taught at Brussels and Kiel before serving as Professor of Sanskrit and Indology at Johns Hopkins University (1931–1958).

Paula Arai is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned degrees from Kalamazoo College and Harvard University. She has held faculty positions at Vanderbilt, Carleton College, Louisiana State University, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Paulina Kolata is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Manchester and held posts at Manchester, Chester, Manchester Metropolitan, Lund, Copenhagen, and an assistant professorship at Harvard University (2025).
Paulina Koniuch is a Buddhist studies and archaeology scholar. She completed her bachelor's degree at the University of Warsaw between 2017 and 2020 and became a faculty member there in 2023.

Paulinus of St. Bartholomew studied at Charles University, the Sapienza, and Collegio San Pancrazio. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he was a missionary in Malabar, rector at Saint Joseph's Pontifical Seminary, and later prefect of studies at the Pontifical Urban University.
Pavankumar Satuluri is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and computational studies. He has held positions at Chinmaya Vishwavidyapeeth and the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee.

Pavel Grintser was an Indologist who studied at Moscow State University under Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson. He later worked at the Gorky Institute of World Literature from 1958 to 2009 and at the Russian State University for the Humanities from 1992 to 2009.

Indologist and linguist Pavel Jakovlevič Petrov studied at Moscow, St. Petersburg, and Berlin under Robert Lenz and Franz Bopp. He served as professor of Sanskrit at Kazan University (1841–1851) and professor of Oriental languages at Moscow University (1852–1875).

Pavel Konstantinovich Portnyagin was a scholar of Tibetan, Iranian, and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University in 1932 and later worked as a translator at the Uzbek Karakul Sheep Breeding Research Institute.
